issue.body:
Previously the per-user child only reexecuted the user systemd instance and restarted `nixos-activation.service`, leaving NixOS-managed user units in `/etc/systemd/user` running stale binaries until the next login.
Options like `systemd.user.services.<name>.restartTriggers` were ineffective.

This PR generalises the existing system-unit comparison loop over a `UnitScope` parameter so the same diff logic covers both `/etc/systemd/system` and `/etc/systemd/user`.
The user-scope child now stops obsolete units, reexecutes and reloads the user systemd, reloads/restarts/starts changed units, and finally runs `nixos-activation.service` (home-manager etc.).

Units are filtered by `FragmentPath` so those shadowed by `~/.config/systemd/user` are left to home-manager to handle.
A second pass after `nixos-activation.service` picks up units that migrate from home-manager to NixOS in the same switch (the opposite direction already works without extra handling).

Split into several commits to make it easier to review:
1. extract the unit comparison loop into `collect_unit_changes()` (no changes besides extracting)
1. introduce a `UnitScope` and parameterise the helpers by it (no behaviour change, only a system scope)
1. introduce a user scope, and implement logic to restart changed user units on switch
1. extend switch test to cover the new functionality
1. handle user units migrating from home-manager to NixOS
1. extend switch test to cover the new functionality

Fixes #246611

pull_request.title: switch-to-configuration-ng: restart changed user units on switch

review_comments.body: This was a bit weird to read at first, I feel it could be a bit more obvious to look at. Perhaps breaking them out into separate variables which are then or'd in the conditional. Just a thought.

This comes verbatim from the existing implementation, I just extracted it into a reusable function.
I agree that we could make it more readable, but I think that I'd prefer to not add any additional changes to this PR as it stands.

> This comes verbatim from the existing implementation, I just extracted it into a reusable function. I agree that we could make it more readable, but I think that I'd prefer to not add any additional changes to this PR as it stands.

It can also be done in a followup if you wish to do it @srounce.

What's the motivation behind this default? I don't think `/run/user/unknown` would be a valid path and that default shouldn't be reachable anyway in my reading? 

At least not if the users switch child is started conventionally from switch-configuration-ng, where you pass XDG_RUNTIME_DIR.

If we want to be extra defensive we could check that the runtime dir is non-empty and exists.

nit: I don't think it's ideal to duplicate those regexes in the source here. Maybe LazyLock or such would be worth it?

(I also just noticed that template_unit_re might technically be wrong? I believe systemd unit instance names are allowed to contain "." (period), which would cause the second group to mismatch?)

Shouldn't we track failed user jobs above and return an error if any failed, like we do for jobs in the system scope?

Or is it a conscious decision to not do that? If so, a comment might be useful as it's a noticeable difference from the user scope.

With the current implementation, a user wouldn't be able to know whether the (user scope) switch was successful without parsing the logs, no?

(If changed, the test could include a failing unit in the user scope as well)
Yeah, that var is set before we fork the per-user child, so it should always be set. Replaced by a simple `expect` now.
For the period, I think you're right, but I'd rather not make that change here, we can open a separate PR for that.
Good point, I refactored that bit.

reviews.body: I see no issues with this personally, the only thing that would be a worry is modular services because it depends on systemd, but that can be in a followup when modular services can popular.
Have kicked the tyres on it in my config and it works nicely.
Very nice, thank you very much! I do appreciate the test coverage & mindful handling of of home-manager migrations :)
